title: 2022 HMMT February Guts Problem 4
statement:
For a real number \(x\), let \([x]\) be \(x\) rounded to the nearest integer and \(\langle x\rangle\) be \(x\) rounded to the nearest tenth. Real numbers \(a\) and \(b\) satisfy \(\langle a\rangle+[b]=98.6\) and \([a]+\langle b\rangle=99.3\). Compute the minimum possible value of \([10(a+b)]\).
(Here, any number equally between two integers or tenths of integers, respectively, is rounded up. For example, \([-4.5]=-4\) and \(\langle 4.35\rangle=4.4\).)

solutions.text:
Without loss of generality, let \(a\) and \(b\) have the same integer part or integer parts that differ by at most 1 , as we can always repeatedly subtract 1 from the larger number and add 1 to the smaller to get another solution.
Next, we note that the decimal part of \(a\) must round to .6 and the decimal part of \(b\) must round to .3 . We note that \((a, b)=(49.55,49.25)\) is a solution and is clearly minimal in fractional parts, giving us \([10(a+b)]=988\).
